nodes.statement: The archon-physics v0.2 entrypoint exposes the locked finite periodic lattice, positive-mass algebra, Hamiltonian scaling, finite normal modes, modal equipartition and entropy observables, ENNReal hitting times, local microscopic dynamics, conservation laws conditional on the ODE, and effective kinetic rescaling APIs, with no custom axiom, sorry, or admit.

nodes.title: Infinite iid mass and phase ensemble
nodes.statement: Construct one probability space carrying an infinite iid mass sequence with common law supported on [mMinus,mPlus] subset (0,infinity), an independent sequence of Haar-uniform phases, and finite-N restriction maps. The canonical RandomEnsemble and IIDMassPhaseEnsemble now kernel-check the infinite iid laws, Haar phases, block independence, finite restrictions, and support bounds. The two-band profile supplies a nonnegative unit-mass macroscopic rank profile, fixed separation from uniform, a 3/M pointwise bound, and vanishing energy on every o(M) soft layer. The remaining obligation is a measurable dependent initial-state adapter realizing that profile and the phases while removing translation position and total momentum and satisfying one uniform energy shell.

nodes.title: Reduced spectrum and measurable mode data
nodes.statement: For N at least two, identify the one-dimensional translation kernel and the N-1 positive sector, and construct measurable ordered frequencies and basis-free modal-energy data. Local kernel proofs now give continuous measurable ordered eigenvalues, globally measurable Lagrange projectors, and exact projector identities on simple spectrum. For canonical iid Uniform[4/5,6/5] masses the complete ordered spectrum is almost surely simple, there is a unique random zero-mode index, positivity holds exactly off that index, and every fixed ordered-mode energy is globally measurable. The spectrum/projector/zero-mode adapter is kernel-closed; only its use along the still-missing global random flow remains downstream.

nodes.title: Mode transform and interaction tensor
nodes.statement: Define Q, P, and complex mode amplitudes on the reduced spectrum; prove the inverse transform, harmonic-energy decomposition, the exact nonlinear interaction-tensor expansion and permutation symmetry, without asserting that every random coupling coefficient is nonzero. The local Physlib bridge kernel-checks the physical Hamilton equations through mass weighting and tensor forcing to interaction- and Schrodinger-picture finite-time Duhamel identities. A new projector outer-product formula constructs globally measurable basis-free squared ordered interaction tensors and normalized physical vertex weights, almost surely equal to the existing eigenbasis vertex square for canonical iid masses. A measurable signed amplitude-level eigenframe still remains for pathwise interaction-picture amplitudes, but second-order collision weights no longer require it.

nodes.title: Concrete coercive cubic-leading global flow
nodes.statement: For fixed kappa and beta with beta greater than 2*kappa^2/9, use U_g(x)=x^2/2+(kappa*g/3)x^3+(beta*g^2/4)x^4 and prove coercivity. Local kernel proofs construct fixed-mass two-sided energy-conserving trajectories, a mass-uniform gauge Poincare bound, and a compact joint mass-inverse-mass energy shell in one ambient phase space. The reduced trajectory is now exactly embedded in that common space; reciprocal mass, both gauges, energy-shell invariance, and a uniform cutoff radius are proved. The canonical jointly measurable global cutoff flow agrees for all time with the true uncut reduced Hamiltonian trajectory. The deterministic and parameter-uniform global-flow adapter is kernel-closed; random initial-data packaging remains downstream.

nodes.title: Jointly measurable random microscopic flow
nodes.statement: Combine the fixed ensemble, measurable initial-state adapter, and coercive global dynamics into a jointly measurable sample-and-time trajectory with continuous paths and the required invariants. Local kernel proofs now provide joint compactness of the canonical mass box and energy shell, the exact reduced-to-parametric ODE embedding, reciprocal mass and gauge invariants, a uniform cutoff radius, and a canonical jointly measurable global flow that agrees for all time with the true uncut reduced trajectory. A consumer specializes this construction to masses in [4/5,6/5] and inverse masses in [5/6,5/4]. Composition with the still-pending measurable initial-profile adapter is the remaining random-model packaging step; the global flow construction itself is kernel-closed.

nodes.title: Measurable full-mode equipartition observable
nodes.statement: On all N-1 nonzero harmonic modes, prove measurability of modal energies, late-window averages, normalization, and the l1 distance to uniform energy. The physical ordered observable is defined basis-free as (normSq(P_k M^(-1/2)p)+lambda_k normSq(P_k sqrt(M)q))/2, is globally measurable and nonnegative, and its full sum equals the original physical harmonic Hamiltonian. The canonical global flow is now composed with this observable: the full profile, positive-frequency mask, and positive-mode finite sum are jointly measurable in sample and time, and every compatible realization agrees for all time with the true uncut reduced orbit. The reduced momentum gauge makes the unique zero-mode energy exactly zero, so the positive sum equals the full modal energy. The remaining F1 observable work is the dependent random initial adapter plus late-window normalization/distance and hitting-time assembly.

The finite-network continuation layer is now kernel-checked: the collision field is C1, nonnegative rates make every nonnegative-orthant boundary coordinate inward, exact triad resonance conserves total kinetic energy, strictly positive frequencies turn the nonnegative energy shell into an explicit sup-norm bound, automatic negative-part control preserves the nonnegative cone, and cutoff continuation constructs an actual global forward solution of the untruncated network equation from every nonnegative initial action. The marked bounded-Lipschitz interface amplifies a test error epsilon_j by at most T_j/(2*pi)+T_j^2/pi, so epsilon_j*(T_j+T_j^2)->0 suffices for resonance-action transfer. nodes.title: Exact random collision-kernel identification
nodes.statement: For the fixed iid mass law and cubic-leading coercive lattice, prove convergence in probability of marked empirical spectral, coupling, and resonance data to exactly the CollisionData used by F2. The scalar profile, complete positive-mode measures, sign-gauge invariance, measurability, physical eigenbasis equality, and marked bounded-Lipschitz transfer are kernel-checked. Exact finite projector/Fourier/resolvent factorization reduces the collision transform to one-leg spectral kernels. The varying-size Levy bridge, uniform compact support/tightness, exact Sherman-Morrison update with an automatically discharged off-spectrum denominator, and single- and finite-mass threshold-count Hamming sensitivity are proved. Bounded differences has been derived from scalar Hoeffding and finite-product Fubini inside Lean: the normalized canonical threshold count has two-sided deviation probability at most 2*exp(-2*N*epsilon^2) around its own finite-volume expectation. Exact trace identities and IID strong laws identify the first two normalized harmonic spectral moments almost surely: trace(H_N)/N tends to 5*log(3/2), while trace(H_N^2)/N tends to 25/6+(25/2)*log(3/2)^2. Generic finite-rank gluing is now specialized to the actual periodic weighted cycle: an explicit ZMod-to-Fin-to-block reindex writes the length n+m cycle as the two smaller periodic cycles plus four signed rank-one boundary terms, hence every threshold-count defect is at most four. This almost-subadditivity now proves convergence of the finite-volume expectation centers at every fixed threshold; McDiarmid concentration then gives convergence in probability to a deterministic scalar IDS value together with an eventual exponential tail, without a continuity-point assumption. For the marked one-leg kernel, the apparent inverse-square-root zero-mode singularity has been removed exactly; the regularized cosine and sine weights are continuous, zero-constant polynomial weights satisfy p(B*B^T)=B*q(B^T*B)*B^T, and the resulting periodic kernel has finite propagation plus finite-window extensionality. The complex Fourier leg splits exactly into regularized cosine and sine components. Continuous zero-constant Weierstrass approximation is proved, and fixed-window polynomial entries and their three-leg products are measurable, uniformly bounded local observables with almost-sure IID spatial strong laws. A deterministic block-remainder theorem lifts convergence along window-width multiples to the ordinary prefix average at every natural volume. The physical cubic tensor has an extensive square lower bound, and the per-site normalized positive collision measure has a realization- and volume-independent positive mass lower bound on simple spectrum. The remaining open core is the deterministic periodic-interior-to-window reindex, volume-uniform continuous-weight three-leg approximation error, the resulting full varying-size random marked spectral-kernel limit, convergence and uniqueness of its collision-measure shape, and a quantitative probability rate compatible with the joint N,g limit.

nodes.title: Full-spectrum infrared control and collision nondegeneracy
nodes.statement: For the exact limiting collision data, control the acoustic edge after removing only the translation mode, prove collision-network connectivity/nondegeneracy, and establish the F2 analytic bounds. Local proofs give exact single-leg l2 scaling and normalizedVertex^2 <= omega0*omega1*omega2/8. The clean cycle has the full multiplicity-counted spectrum 4*sin(pi*j/N)^2 and explicit acoustic threshold-count envelopes; frozen random spectra inherit deterministic count sandwiches and one- or finitely-many mass replacements obey exact threshold-count sensitivity bounds. The periodic transfer polynomial has exact normalized linear coefficient equal to the empirical mass mean, converging almost surely to one, and the first two normalized harmonic trace moments have explicit almost-sure limits. Finite Fubini plus Parseval gives the exact full cubic tensor-square identity; frozen inverse masses imply the extensive lower bound (125/36)*N. Combining the uniform frequency ceiling with simple spectrum gives a raw positive collision mass at least c*N, so the natural per-site collision measure has a uniform strictly positive total mass. This rules out vanishing total collision weight but does not locate that weight near zero mismatch. Resonant-state density/Jacobian compensation, on-shell or broadened-resonance lower bounds, N-stable connectivity, invariant classification, and weighted coercivity for the exact limiting random kernel remain open.
